item.title: World-famous Catholic shrine torched, 'Devil in a skirt' scrawled on Virgin Mary statue
item.description: Surveillance footage shows a man pouring gasoline on the altar at St. James Church as the Medjugorje shrine was vandalized days before a major festival.
item.content:encoded:
A man has been arrested after one of the world's most famous Catholic pilgrimage sites was vandalized and partially set on fire, with a statue of the Virgin Mary defaced and the words "Devil in a skirt" scrawled across its pedestal in black, according to reports.

Bosnian police arrested a suspect Tuesday in connection with the overnight vandalism and arson at the Shrine of Our Lady in Medjugorje, according to Vatican News.

Authorities have not released the man's identity as investigators work to determine a motive and whether he was responsible for other incidents reported at the shrine that same night, the outlet said.

NIGERIAN PASTOR HIGHLIGHTED BY TRUMP SAYS HE’S NEXT AFTER MILITIA KILLS HIS RELATIVES

Police were called around 4:30 a.m. July 27 after the face and hands of the statue of the Virgin Mary on Apparition Hill, also known as Podbrdo, were found covered in black paint.

The pedestal at the foot of the statue was spray-painted with the English phrase "Devil in a skirt," while other graffiti and the statue's hands were painted black.

An outdoor altar nearby was also set on fire near St. James Church, the outlet said.

Surveillance footage reportedly at that location showed a man pouring what investigators believe was gasoline onto the altar before setting it ablaze. The fire was extinguished.

REPORT DETAILS RISING PRESSURE ON UNDERGROUND CATHOLICS AS CHINA DENIES CRACKDOWN

The two attacks came just days before Medjugorje's annual youth prayer festival, which is expected to draw more than 50,000 pilgrims from around the world.

In a statement Tuesday, the Medjugorje Parish Office condemned the vandalism and urged Catholics to respond with "prayer, fasting, and forgiveness" rather than anger.

"It is with great sadness that we received the news of the act of vandalism," the parish said.

Church officials also said cleanup and repairs began immediately so the damaged prayer sites could once again welcome pilgrims.

"The affected areas are being cleaned and restored as quickly as possible," the parish said, thanking volunteers for helping preserve the shrine as "a place of encounter with God, a place of peace."

CATHOLIC NUNS SUE NEW YORK, SAY ASSISTED SUICIDE LAW FORCES THEM TO VIOLATE THEIR FAITH

Rather than calling for retribution, the parish urged the faithful to pray for those responsible.

"We pray for the conversion of the hearts of those who committed this act," the statement said, asking that God "touch them with His grace and lead them on the path of goodness."

The parish also appealed for peace, encouraging Catholics "not to return evil for evil," but instead to bear witness through "love, forgiveness and hope."

Despite the attack, officials said the shrine remains open, and its regular schedule of Mass and prayer services will continue as planned.

Located about 85 miles southwest of Sarajevo, Medjugorje became one of the world's best-known Catholic pilgrimage destinations after six children and teenagers reported seeing apparitions of the Virgin Mary there in 1981.

The Vatican gave the green light for Catholics to continue flocking to Medjugorje offering its approval for devotion at one of the most contested sites of Roman Catholic practice in recent years, The Associated Press reported Tuesday.

item.title: Spanish soccer player makes good on his promise to get tattoo of team's manager after World Cup win
item.description: Marc Cucurella followed through on his pre-tournament pledge, getting a tattoo of manager Luis de la Fuente holding the World Cup trophy on his arm.
item.content:encoded:
Spain is still taking a well-deserved victory lap after locking up the World Cup title earlier this month, and for one player, that involved getting some fresh ink.

And what better way to commemorate the win than by getting the World Cup trophy permanently drawn on your body?

I'll tell you one: getting your manager's big ol' mug holding the World Cup trophy permanently drawn on your body, which is what Spain's Marc Cucurella did.

SPAIN BEATS ARGENTINA TO WIN 2026 FIFA WORLD CUP BEHIND FERRAN TORRES' EXTRA-TIME GOAL

Even before the tournament started, Cucurella pledged to get a tattoo of his manager's face if the team went all the way.

He may have thought he was in the clear when Spain opened the tournament with a 0-0 draw against Cape Verde, but that turned out to be the only blemish on their World Cup record.

Spain defeated reigning champs Argentina for the title on July 19, and now Cucurella is making good on his promise.

There had to be a point, as Spain was closing in on the final, where Cucurella was hoping everyone had forgotten about all of this tattoo business.

FERRAN TORRES SPORTS 'MAKE SPAIN GREAT AGAIN' HAT SIMILAR TO TRUMP'S SLOGAN AT WORLD CUP HOMECOMING PARADE

Unfortunately for him, the internet doesn't forget.

But it's a unique memento from Spain's World Cup run, and good on him for sticking to his word.

I think he's going to get irritated in a hurry when he has to keep fielding the questions, "Who is that old guy on your arm?" over and over and over.

Hell, he might just want to get a second tattoo right under that just says, "Before you ask me, it's Spanish national soccer team manager Luis de la Fuente."

item.title: Trump says heroic teen lifeguard who saved boy from towering waves deserves White House honor
item.description: Trump says the California teen who repeatedly disappeared beneath crashing waves while saving a child showed extraordinary courage worthy of national recognition.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump on Tuesday praised the teenage lifeguard who went viral after rescuing a young boy from towering waves in Santa Cruz, California, saying he wants to invite the teen to the White House and potentially award him a high civilian honor.

The lifeguard, identified as 16-year-old Ryder on social media, was captured in a heart-stopping video Saturday battling massive surf as he repeatedly disappeared beneath crashing waves while maintaining a relentless grip on the child he was rescuing.

After seeing the dramatic rescue, Trump said the teen deserved national recognition. 

"We’re going to bring this heroic young man, and his family, into the White House with, perhaps, the boy he saved, to give him a High Civilian Honor. Very brave, he deserves it!" Trump said in a post on X. 

HEROIC 16-YEAR-OLD LIFEGUARD RESCUES CHILD FROM MONSTER SURF IN HEART-STOPPING VIDEO

Hours earlier, Eric Trump also praised the rescue on social media, calling for the teen to receive the nation's highest civilian recognition. 

"Give this 16-year-old lifeguard the highest civilian honor. This is truly the best of America! Well done!" he said. 

The rescue drew thousands of reactions online, with many praising Ryder for battling powerful waves that appeared too dangerous even for bystanders who attempted to help. 

One person claiming to have witnessed the rescue said it lasted far longer than the viral video showed. Beachgoers reportedly formed a human chain in an effort to help before it was eventually broken apart by the pounding surf, according to social media users. 

MAN, WOMAN KILLED IN RIP CURRENT AS LIFEGUARD SHORTAGE LEAVES DANGER ZONES IN BEACH DESTINATION

After pulling the child safely onto the beach, Ryder reportedly sprinted past his lifeguard tower to get aid as paramedics arrived to evaluate the boy, the witness said. Despite the dramatic rescue, Ryder later returned to duty and continued watching over beachgoers for the rest of the evening. 

The rescue may have come during Ryder's first season as a lifeguard. California State Parks requires state lifeguards to be at least 16 years old.

Another social media user who said she knew Ryder emphasized how extraordinary the rescue was. 

"I’m not sure how many people know how hard it is to hold onto someone like that in the ocean, during these heavy conditions and pounding shore break. This lifeguard handled it like a pro, pulled him in most of the way solo and never gave up. Taht is a feat in itself, especially in those conditions. A true Hero & waterman. I seriously hope he gets recognized for this," the user said. 

Other people claiming to have witnessed the incident said the surf had initially appeared relatively calm, with many beachgoers standing at the water's edge when a massive wave suddenly crashed ashore. 

"It was so big it nearly reached us by our things all the way up the beach!" the witness said. 

Seabright Beach is known for its powerful shore break, with waves shaped by swells arriving from multiple directions, creating hazardous conditions even for experienced swimmers.

item.title: Hot bobsledder Desi Johnson gets in touch with nature, ‘Shark Lady’ breaks world record & woke brewery busted
item.description: NFL training camp is here, Minocqua Brewing Company loses its permit, and bobsledder Desi Johnson escapes to Kyrgyzstan for a nature retreat.
item.content:encoded:
'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com.

It's a beautiful day, Nightcaps family.

You know why? I'll tell you. Because as of today, Tuesday, July 28 in the Year of our Lord 2026, all 32 NFL teams have reported to Training Camp.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

That means in just a couple short weeks (well, one week if you count the Hall of Fame Game), preseason football will be on our TV screens. And shortly afterward, college ball will consume our Saturdays. As God intended.

Not trying to wish away anyone's summer — my colleagues Joe Kinsey and SeanJo would be very disappointed in me if I did that — but MAN. Call me Hank Jr. because I am ready for some football.

Speaking of summer, I'm still in Minocqua, Wisconsin, at my mother-in-law's house. Nashville feels like the devil's sweaty armpit this time of year, so it's nice to get a little bit of cooler weather up here in the Northwoods.

Last week, we shot up to the Minnesota North Shore for some hiking. Goodness, it's beautiful up there. And they have some great local breweries, too.

My dog is way too cool for his own good.

But you didn't come here for my family photos. You came to find out what's going on on the internet today. So let's get to it, shall we?

Pop open a Fulton 300 IPA, chuck your work laptop into Lake Superior and let's go.

An update on the wackos at Minocqua Brewing Company

Speaking of beer...

If you've been reading my Nightcaps for a while, you might remember me talking about the Minocqua Brewing Company. It's "downtown" Minocqua (I'm using that term loosely) inside an old gas station from the 1930s.

Actually, a pretty cool little building. Perfect spot for a brewery. Shame the owner, Kirk Bangstad, is a certified nutcase.

Now, I pride myself in my ability to get along with people who don't agree with me, but I assure you Kirk has no desire to get along with me. Or likely anyone reading this, for that matter.

He's as far left as they come. There are signs plastered all over the outside of the joint that say "least popular place in town," "drink MAGA tears" and "Antifa parking only."

The beers are named things like "AOC IPA," "The Resistance," "Choice," "Fascist Tears" and their Mexican lager, "It'll Always Be the Gulf of Mexico to Me." They also sell their own coffee and coffee stout, called "WOKE."

To their credit, that's actually a pretty clever name for coffee.

I digress. This guy isn't insufferable because he's a lib. I know lots of libs, and I like them just fine. He's insufferable because he's awful.

Kirk is always at war with the city and other local businesses, and he's been charged with multiple legal offenses, including criminal defamation, harassment, bail jumping, disorderly conduct, and (last but not least) defrauding donors to his super PAC by funneling thousands of dollars to himself to pay for his legal fees. Last year he tried to hijack the 4th of July parade. I don't have the time or patience to list his whole rap sheet.

But if it tells you anything, this dude is such a turd he even named one of his beers after his lawyer. It has the guy's face on the can and everything. 

Well, this week, his permit got pulled. Turns out, Kirk has been illegally transporting beer from Illinois without securing the proper permits or paying the appropriate taxes.

Not paying taxes! Imagine that.

The revocation is effective Aug. 4 — next Tuesday. Still, he has no intention of shutting down.

"They’ll have to pry me out of my taprooms before I stop selling beer to thirsty progressives who come to visit us," he wrote, per the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel.

So I'll be sure to walk by the brewery today and wave to ol' Kirk before he likely gets hauled off by the authorities.

I'm sure his lawyer, Fred Melms (aka "Grateful Fred Red Ale") will be on the case.

Bobsledder Desi Johnson gets in touch with nature

I'm not the only one escaping the hustle and bustle of the city. Desi Johnson — a Team Australia bobsledder who went viral during the Winter Olympics for being hot, as one does — got away on a nature retreat in rural Kyrgyzstan this week.

Gotta admit, Kyrgyzstan is not a country I've ever thought twice about. Or once, actually. But it looks beautiful.

I have no idea what the bobsledding season looks like. As far as I know, people only bobsled once every four years. But I'm sure there's some sort of training or competitions involved in the interim.

Regardless, Desi seems to be keeping busy traveling, getting outdoors, running sprints and selling workout clothing.

Someone's ready for French Alps 2030!

'Shark Lady' breaks record for most shark tattoos

Hold on, let me clarify: She has broken the world record for "most sharks tattooed on the body (female)" with 106.

I know what you're thinking: Amber, does that mean some dude out there has 107 shark tattoos?

And the answer is no. Or if he does, he hasn't come forward. I guess the folks over at the Guinness Book of World Records wanted to specify female body just to leave the door open for a man who wanted his own shot at glory.

I swear there is a Guinness World Record for everything. Somewhere out there, someone just broke the world record for "most Busch Lights (corn can) drank in a northern Illinois garage on an overcast Monday in July."

And yes, I have one specific person in mind for that one.

SHARK WEEK HOST FORREST GALANTE EXPLAINS WHY CRUSHING BEERS IN THE OCEAN IS A BAD IDEA

True story, though, remember a couple of weeks ago when I was telling y'all about the mountain of dumb PR pitches that end up in my email inbox daily?

Case in point: I got an email from an organization (a movement? a nonprofit? a cult? I truly have no idea) called "World Clap Day" — proudly announcing that its founder, Andrea, completed 24 consecutive hours of live clapping, setting a new world record. That's 149,216 claps!

I bet her hands hurt so bad.

You know, when I first read that email, I thought to myself, Why in the hell would these people think I would write about this? And here I am, writing about it.

Touché, clapping cult.

Wow, I really got in the weeds there. Back to the shark tattoo chick.

Her name is Emily Morrison, and she goes by "Shark Lady Emily" on social media.

A fitting moniker, to be sure.

And don't you dare try to tell Emily to stop getting shark tattoos. Because you know what she has to say about that?

"I will not stop getting shark tattoos."

If you're really into this sort of thing, Emily will be featured on My Strange Addiction as part of Discovery's "Shark Week."

I've only watched that show one time, and it was an episode about a lady who can't stop eating toilet paper. So when you look at it that way, Emily's actually killing it.

Let's open the mailbag.

🐦 Twitter/X: @TheAmberHarding

📸 Instagram: @amberharding

Fred H. writes: When it gets hot the cows go in the pond. One of these is not a cow.

Amber:

I don't know what you're talking about. That's obviously just a very small cow. Who barks.

Jon C. writes: Haven’t done a Hyrox race, yet. Had some friends do the one in Houston earlier this year and we were looking at doing the Nashville one together. Tickets might seem to be an issue.

However, if you want something very similar and more accessible, do a DekaFit race. It is a 5k with a workout station every 500m. So just like Hyrox except the workout stations are different. To me, Hyrox has more aerobic stations while Deka has more strength stations. I’ve done a few DekaFits and they are tough. For what it’s worth, Deka is an off shoot of Spartan Races, the trail running obstacle course race. 

Amber:

For those who missed it, last week I explained that a friend of mine asked me to do a HYROX race with her. Apparently, it's hella impossible to get tickets to compete in HYROX events, though — especially the upcoming Nashville race in December.

Everybody wants to come to Nashville.

So maybe we'll look into DEKA instead. From what I've seen (and from how Jon described it), DEKA is more up my alley anyway. I'm more of a lifter than a runner.

But I still do the latter, begrudgingly.

item.title: Minnesota Vikings suspend defensive backs coach Gerald Alexander after DWI guilty plea
item.description: Gerald Alexander's blood alcohol level was more than twice the Minnesota legal limit, leading to a guilty plea and and a three-week team suspension.
item.content:encoded:
Another NFL assistant coach is being disciplined by his team after facing driving under the influence allegations, this time with Minnesota Vikings defensive backs coach Gerald Alexander being suspended by the team.

The Vikings announced Tuesday that Alexander has been suspended for three weeks after he pleaded guilty to driving while intoxicated earlier this month. Alexander's blood alcohol level was 0.169, or more than twice Minnesota's legal limit, on an initial breathalyzer test, according to the charging statement.

Alexander, hired in February as the team's passing game coordinator as well as defensive backs coach, was arrested in April, and his guilty plea came on July 16.

NFL SUSPENDS ARIZONA CARDINALS EXECUTIVE FOR VIOLATING GAMBLING POLICY, LEAKING DRAFT INFO

Alexander pleaded guilty to third-degree DWI, a misdemeanor, and paid $603 in fines and fees. He was assigned 48 hours of community service and will be on probation for two years.

Alexander's club suspension began on July 24, although it was not announced then. It will run through Aug. 13.

"Following Gerald’s arrest earlier this spring, we remained in communication with the NFL while awaiting the outcome of the legal process," the Vikings said in a statement. "We take these situations seriously and believe this disciplinary action is appropriate."

The NFL tells Fox News Digital the club suspension will close the matter and Alexander will not be subject to additional league discipline under the personal conduct policy.

Alexander, who previously worked under Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores in Miami when Flores was the head coach, also released a statement through the team.

"I take full responsibility for the situation I put myself in and apologize for not meeting the mark," Alexander said. "I know it’s unacceptable. I understand the suspension and am committed to learning from the matter and ensuring I come back a better version of myself."

TONY ROMO ARRESTED IN MILWAUKEE FOR ALLEGED OWI OFFENSE: REPORT

Alexander is the second NFL assistant coach to face team discipline for offseason troubles with DWI.

The Washington Commanders on Monday announced the firing of assistant coach Ben Steele just days before the start of training camp.

Steele, who was serving as the team's tight ends coach, was hired by the Commanders this offseason.

"We are parting ways with tight ends coach Ben Steele. The team will have no further comment at this time," the Commanders said in a statement.

The Athletic reported that Steele was arrested on suspicion of DWI in June. He is facing an additional charge for refusing a blood/breath test and obstructing or resisting an officer without force, per the report.

Steele had previously been under suspension by the Commanders.

These two issues coming to light in the same week suggest some coaches may need more extensive training or onboarding to make clear the pitfalls of drinking — even away from the club.

item.title: Haley Stevens shreds Abdul El-Sayed: 'We don't need a celebrity candidate'
item.description: Haley Stevens repeatedly branded Abdul El-Sayed the "celebrity" candidate during Monday's heated Michigan Senate Democratic debate before the primary.
item.content:encoded:
Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich., repeatedly called Abdul El-Sayed the "celebrity" candidate in the Michigan Senate race during Monday's Senate Democratic debate, arguing that El-Sayed's podcast, books and political activism pale in comparison to her time in Congress.

The race between Stevens and El-Sayed has become a microcosm of the battle over the Democratic Party's future. On Aug. 4, Democratic voters will decide whether to back Stevens, who has the support of the Democratic establishment, or El-Sayed, a socialist-supported challenger who has called for abolishing ICE and is strongly critical of the United States' support for Israel.

In her opening remarks, Stevens rattled off her qualifications as the Democratic Party's best chance of winning the Senate race, pointing to flipping her seat in 2018, being named Michigan's most effective Democratic lawmaker by the Center for Effective Lawmaking in 2025 and being endorsed by Democratic Michigan Democratic Gov. Gretchen Whitmer.

"My only focus is you," Stevens said. "Abdul is running for celebrity. Republicans are propping up his campaign, and Mike Rogers, just the other day said in a secret phone call that he made it easier for him to win, that he's the one he wants to run against."

DEM CIVIL WAR HITS PRIMARY DEBATE STAGE IN FIERY BATTLEGROUND SHOWDOWN: 'WHAT ARE YOU HIDING?'

Stevens was referring to a phone conversation Republican candidate Mike Rogers had with supporters last month in which he said his campaign would be in "good shape" if El-Sayed were the nominee.

"Look, this isn't about the D.C. or New York influencer crowd," Stevens said. "This is about putting Michigan first."

Later in the debate, Stevens said she is standing up to Trump's "abuses of powers," while taking a dig at Abdul by saying she's doing so without "shouting into a bullhorn, not getting in front of the first camera I see, but doing the hard work."

SWING-STATE POLL SPELLS TROUBLE FOR FAR LEFT AS SCHUMER-BACKED CANDIDATE DOMINATES WITH CRITICAL VOTING BLOCS

"Look, my opponent here, Abdul, he is such a talented guy," Stevens said, referring to his three books and his podcast America Dissected. "He's had all this attention, but the deal is, we don't need a celebrity candidate. We don't need a celebrity."

Stevens then pointed to her six years in the House of Representatives, saying she has been committed to "hard, unglamorous work."

"That's going to stand up to this junk that is wreaking havoc and causing chaos right before our very eyes," Stevens said.

Stevens suggested that Abdul's Senate campaign is just another "rung on the ladder" for him, pointing to his failed 2018 gubernatorial bid.

"It didn't work out, so he started the podcast, he wrote the books, and now he's running for Senate, and he's already bought the website for president," Stevens said.

In response, El-Sayed accused Stevens of "cowardice" over her past votes to increase ICE funding, saying the agency should be completely abolished.

MICHIGAN SENATE CANDIDATE ABDUL EL-SAYED DODGES QUESTION ON WHETHER HE STILL SUPPORTS DEFUNDING THE POLICE

"So yeah, I’m going to take the bullhorn and I’m going to say that I think we need to abolish ICE because I am not afraid of what they’re going to say about me," he said.

He also suggested that Stevens' focus on his public health podcast was a distraction from the issues that matter most to voters, such as affordability.

"Congresswoman, if you enjoy podcasts about public health, I welcome you to take a listen. You seem very concerned about that," El-Sayed said. "I’m more concerned about the fact that people can’t pay for their gas, they can’t pay for their groceries."

The open Senate race in Michigan has garnered national attention, with outside groups spending more than $52 million on the race through mid-July, most of it in support of Stevens, according to an OpenSecrets analysis of FEC reports.

El-Sayed, who is backed by Sen. Bernie Sanders, D-Vt., has painted Stevens as the candidate of large super PACs such as AIPAC, while saying he has not received a single dollar from corporate interests or super PACs. Before running for Congress, El-Sayed served as Wayne County director of Health and Human Services.

Meanwhile, the Republican Party has deemed Michigan to be one of best pickup opportunities in its effort to maintain control of the Senate.

Fox News Digital reached out to El-Sayed and Stevens' campaigns for comment.

item.title: Marcus Mumford says Bible camp sparked decades-long love story with wife Carey Mulligan
item.description: Marcus Mumford revealed on the "SmartLess" podcast how a childhood Bible camp meeting with Carey Mulligan led to their famously private marriage.
item.content:encoded:
Before Marcus Mumford and Carey Mulligan became one of Hollywood's most private couples, they were just two kids who met at Bible camp.

The Mumford & Sons frontman recalled on the "SmartLess" podcast how a chance childhood meeting eventually blossomed into romance years later after the pair reconnected as adults.

The future couple first crossed paths at a church Bible camp, when Mumford was 10 and Mulligan was 12, and became pen pals.

JESSIE JAMES DECKER ON WHY HER MARRIAGE TO ERIC DECKER HASN'T LOST ITS SPARK AFTER FOUR KIDS

"And she still has the journal entry from the day we met where I – my cousin was there, who was two years older, who was age appropriate for her," Mumford recalled. "And he got an eight-and-a-half out of 10. But I, who was definitely not underlined boyfriend material, got a nine out 10."

The flattering review didn't spark an instant romance, but it planted the seed for a relationship that would take years to come together.

He recalled the two "stayed in touch as kids" before reconnecting in their twenties on Facebook. Mulligan bought a ticket to Laura Marling's show years later, where Mumford & Sons was also performing.

LAINEY WILSON ADMITS SHE LIED TO FIANCÉ DUCK HODGES ON THEIR FIRST DATE

"We started shouting sort of an hour before Laura went on and then [Mulligan] was like, 'Oh, Mumford. I knew a kid called Mumford,'" the singer-songwriter recalled.

Mulligan left a note with Mumford's tour manager that had her email address on it and the rest is history.

After dating for roughly five months, Mumford proposed to Mulligan. The two married in front of friends and family in Somerset, England, on April 21, 2012. Mumford and Mulligan share three children together, two daughters and a son.

The couple is notoriously private about their 14-year marriage.

"Marcus is the only thing that’s mine that I can keep totally away, so I try to," Mulligan told Vogue in 2015.

Throughout the years, Mumford and Mulligan have focused on making their marriage "the priority" in their lives.

"We said, ‘The odds are stacked against us. Let’s make that our great work and everything else can come from that, right?’" Mumford told GQ in 2022. "The reason I think people don’t stay married is because they don’t realize how much work it takes."

Mulligan is a British actress known for her roles in "An Education," "Drive," "The Great Gatsby," "Promising Young Woman" and "Maestro," the latter earning her a third Oscar nomination.

Mumford, raised in England, is best known as the lead singer, guitarist and songwriter for Mumford & Sons, the Grammy-winning folk-rock band that helped define the early 2010s folk revival.

item.title: Wisconsin brewery that offered 'free beer' when Trump dies says alcohol permit revoked
item.description: Kirk Bangstad says he will fight the Wisconsin Department of Revenue's revocation of Minocqua Brewing Company's alcohol permit set to take effect Aug. 4.
item.content:encoded:
A Wisconsin brewery known for anti-Trump social media posts, including one promising a free beer promotion upon the death of President Donald Trump, has had its permit to operate in the state revoked by state officials.

The Milwaukee Journal Sentinel reported Monday that liberal activist and brewery owner Kirk Bangstad is "vowing to fight ‘tooth and nail’ after receiving a letter from the state's Department of Revenue revoking Minocqua Brewing Co.'s permit to operate in Wisconsin, according to a July 26 newsletter sent to his supporters."

"As you can imagine, I’m not taking this lying down," Bangstad wrote in a Substack post on Sunday. "We’re going to fight the state of Wisconsin tooth and nail, and once again, they’ll have to pry me out of my taprooms before I stop selling beer to thirsty progressives who come to visit us."

WISCONSIN DEM'S BAR LAMENTS 'WE ALMOST GOT FREE BEER DAY' FOR TRUMP ASSASSINATION

He also asked readers to donate to his legal defense fund, writing, "As usual, fighting to keep my business alive means I have to pay lawyers, and that’s never cheap. Every time this [happens], I rack up $100K in legal bills before we even see a judge. If you can help chip in to the Minocqua Company’s legal defense fund, I’d really appreciate it."

The revocation of the beer license goes into effect on Aug. 4, the Sentinel reported. The business has locations in Madison and Minocqua.

In a statement to Fox News Digital, a spokesperson for the Wisconsin Department of Revenue said, "The Wisconsin Division of Alcohol Beverages is dedicated to the fair and consistent enforcement of alcohol beverages regulations in Wisconsin. The division is required to follow and implement state law, including ensuring permit holders and licensees follow all applicable laws and regulations. The division takes appropriate actions when these laws are not followed."

The spokesperson added, "We can confirm that the Department of Revenue has issued notice of a Brewer's permit revocation for two Minocqua Brewing Company locations and notice of an Alcohol Beverage Warehouse permit revocation for one location. The business has until August 4th to appeal and can operate during the appeal process. Should the business decide to appeal, the next step would be to appeal to the Secretary of the Department of Revenue, who will assign the appeal to a Department of Revenue hearing examiner for their recommendations as to proposed findings of fact and conclusions of law."

The Sentinel reported that state regulators pursued revoking Bangstad's alcohol license after authorities seized canned beer from his company in June, alleging it had been transported from Illinois without the required permits and taxes. The newspaper also reported that Bangstad criticized the proposed action as an excessive response, arguing the alleged tax violations did not warrant shutting down his business.

'FREE BEER' FOR TRUMP DEATH DEM ACTIVIST RUNNING FOR WISCONSIN GOV: 'I WILL WIN' IF THEY SILENCE ME

On Jan. 22, the Minocqua Brewing Company appeared to suggest it would give free beer to patrons if Trump was killed, and while not explicitly using his name, posted on Facebook, "Free beer, all day long the day he dies."

The post continued, "Show us this post when it happens in a few months and we’ll make good on that promise."

The post was updated to say, "we meant the Madison Taproom because that’s open all year, if he dies in the summer, then it’s gonna be the Minocqua Taproom."

In reply to comment on the post, the company also did not refer to Trump by name but said that the post hinted at a high-profile figure when asked whether the timeline for the deal could be moved up earlier.

"Well that's up to you and your ability to act like a cia [sic] agent," the company wrote.

item.title: Democratic Wisconsin gubernatorial candidate doesn't recall 'abolish the Senate' post in 2021, campaign says
item.description: Francesca Hong's campaign said she doesn't recall her 2021 "Abolish the Senate" post and that it's not her current position in a comment to Fox News Digital.

DEM SOCIALIST RUNNING FOR WISCONSIN GOVERNOR PUSHED 'ABOLISHING THE POLICE'

item.title: Supreme Court denies stays for two Florida death row inmates, clearing path for rare double execution
item.description: The Supreme Court denied stays of execution for two Florida death row inmates, clearing the way for the state's first double execution since 1964.
item.content:encoded:
The U.S. Supreme Court denied stays for two Florida death row inmates scheduled to be executed Tuesday, clearing the way for the state to execute the 11th and 12th inmates this year.

The court denied two separate requests for stays in the planned executions.

Former police officer James Duckett, 68, had been scheduled to die at noon on Tuesday, but the execution was delayed awaiting results of the stay requests before the Supreme Court.

THOMAS UNLOADS ON COURT FOR HELPING CONVICTED MURDERER BUT IGNORING 'LAW-ABIDING CITIZENS'

Duckett, according to local media reports, was executed by lethal injection and pronounced dead at 1:19 p.m.

Duckett was convicted of raping and murdering an 11-year-old girl in 1987.

The Supreme Court also denied a separate stay for Dominick Occhicone, an 80-year-old who was convicted of murdering his ex-girlfriend’s parents in 1986.

JUDGE BLOCKS ALABAMA'S NITROGEN GAS EXECUTION METHOD, RULES IT IS UNCONSTITUTIONALLY CRUEL

Occhicone's execution is scheduled for 6 p.m. If executed, he would become the oldest inmate executed in Florida.

If carried out, Occhicone's execution would mark the first time Florida executed two inmates in one day since 1964. It would be just the second double execution in the U.S. in the 2000s and the first since Arkansas executed two inmates in 2007.

Florida executed 19 inmates in 2025, according to a Fox News Digital review of Florida Department of Corrections data. The 11 people the state has executed so far this year are more than double the next closest state, with Texas having executed four inmates this year, according to the Texas Department of Criminal Justice.

item.title: Trump's war on fraud expands as Treasury launches new site with whistleblower incentives
item.description: Treasury's new whistleblower program offers payments to Americans who report fraud, money laundering and sanctions violations through a centralized portal.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: Americans could soon cash in on exposing fraud as President Donald Trump's Treasury Department prepares to launch a program paying whistleblowers, Fox News Digital has learned.

The Treasury Department has created an online tip line that incentivize Americans to bring allegations of fraud directly to the administration in an effort to increase transparency and crack down on abuse of taxpayer dollars. The website encourages people to "blow the whistle on fraud, money laundering and sanctions/tax violations."

And those who report explicit details of legitimate fraudulent transactions could see a pay day for their information.

"Whistleblowers play a critical role in protecting the integrity of our financial system," Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Fox News Digital.

THE WAR ON FRAUD IS HERE, AND VICE PRESIDENT VANCE IS LEADING IT FROM THE FRONT

"Today, on National Whistleblower Day, Treasury launched a new webpage that brings our whistleblower programs together in one place, making it easier to find information and navigate the reporting process," he continued.

Awards for whistleblowers could range between 10% and 30% of the total amount in penalties recovered from successful enforcement operations carried out by the Departments of Treasury and Justice.

The rollout marks the latest step in the Trump administration's broader campaign to root out fraud across federal programs after officials argued billions in taxpayer dollars have been lost to waste, abuse and organized criminal schemes.

The program works alongside the Task Force to Eliminate Fraud — a federal initiative led by Vice President JD Vance that President Donald Trump established by executive order earlier this year. It also mirrors a similar program that was used to root out illicit money movements in Minnesota in the midst of the Feeding Our Futures fraud scandal.

The new website consolidates Treasury's existing whistleblower programs into a single public portal, allowing for fraud report submissions to go through one website that routes tips to the department's various enforcement bureaus.

FEDERAL GOVERNMENT’S LANDLORD JOINS VANCE FRAUD CRACKDOWN AS WHITE HOUSE WIDENS HUNT: 'CRITICAL FORCE'

It also serves as a hub for Treasury's broader anti-fraud campaign, with initiatives ranging from Internal Revenue Service (IRS) fraud investigations and sanctions enforcement to financial institution alerts, whistleblower protections and the White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, led by Vance.

"Fighting fraud is a core national security and taxpayer protection mission for Treasury," a Treasury spokesperson told Fox News Digital. "Secretary Bessent has directed the Department to modernize its tools, strengthen partnerships with financial institutions and law enforcement, and aggressively pursue those who steal from the American people. Treasury is committed to preventing fraud before it occurs, disrupting criminal networks that exploit government programs, and holding bad actors accountable."

Both the new whistleblower program and anti-fraud task force were created in response to the massive fraud scandal in Minnesota that triggered investigations that later exposed taxpayer dollar abuse statewide.

The exposed fraud included allegations that the state’s Somali community was exploiting social services to send millions of dollars to those unqualified to receive financial assistance, including al Qaeda-linked terror groups.

"President Trump has been clear that Americans have a right to know that their tax dollars are not being diverted to fund acts of global terror or to fund luxury cars for fraudsters," a statement from Bessent featured on the new website reads. "At Treasury, we follow the money."

JACOB FREY PRAISES SOMALI COMMUNITY AS MINNESOTA FACES RENEWED SCRUTINY OVER FRAUD INVESTIGATIONS

"We did it with the mafia, we have done it with all the cartels, and we’re doing it with the Somali fraudsters," he went on in the public statement. "We are going to offer whistleblower payments to anyone who wants to tell us the who, what, when, where and how this fraud and money laundering occurred."

The portal provides direct reporting links to Treasury bureaus including the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network, the IRS and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, allowing tips to be routed to the agency best equipped to investigate them.

Treasury has not yet specified how whistleblower payments will be calculated or which cases would qualify for financial rewards.

item.title: Charley Hull pulls off savage lottery prank on her caddie at Women's British Open
item.description: Charley Hull gave caddie Adam Woodward a fake scratch-off lottery ticket in the player's lounge at Royal Lytham, and his reaction was priceless.
item.content:encoded:
Charley Hull isn't one to take things too seriously, both on and off the golf course, and she's keeping things incredibly lighthearted ahead of the final major championship of the year.

Speaking with the media ahead of this week's Women's British Open at Royal Lytham & St Annes Golf Club in England, Hull shared a quick story involving her caddie Adam Woodward. While Woodward has been on Hull's bag for over a decade and has had great success alongside her, he may have questioned calling it quits after the prank Hull pulled off on him.

As Hull went on to explain, she popped into a prank shop in town the day prior and picked up a fake scratch-off lottery ticket. She gave the ticket over to Woodward in the player's lounge at Royal Lytham on Tuesday morning. Naturally, he scratched it off right then and there and thought he had won $100,000.

PAULINA GRETZKY HIT THE GOLF COURSE DRESSED FOR SUCCESS AND WON, BROOKS NADER IN HER BAYWATCH RED & A SQUIRREL

Based on Hull's recounting of the story, she led him to believe he had become a big winner for quite some time.

"I went to a prank shop in Blackpool last night and got some scratch cards. We go into the player lounge this morning and I was like 'Hey, I got some scratch cards from the shop,'" Hull explained nonchalantly.

"He's scratching it, scratching it, scratching, and he's like 'Oh my gosh, I've won' and he's taken his hat off, he's taken his glasses off. He's literally running around the player's lounge saying 'I've won $100,000, I'm taking today off.'

"He was sweating, he was trembling, he couldn't believe his luck, and we had to tell him it was fake and he nearly quit the job," Hull concluded with a laugh.

While it would come as a surprise to no one to hear Hull randomly tell the story of her savage prank on her caddie, it came up amid her being completely transparent about her love for playing for such large purses at major championships.

"I'm not going to lie," Hull said. "That's why I think I play so well in the majors. Even if I'm quite a lot behind, I am like, make loads of birdies today, extra dollars, for me and him to get."

Hull, who enters the week ranked seventh in the world, has finished runner-up in three of the five major championships on the women's side in her career, and certainly wouldn't mind earning her maiden major title in her home country come Sunday.

item.title: More than 12,000 pounds of bacon recalled after USDA issues highest-risk alert
item.description: Federal food safety officials have recalled more than 12,000 pounds of imported bacon after discovering the products entered the country without undergoing a mandatory inspection.
item.content:encoded:
More than 12,000 pounds of imported smoked bacon have been recalled, according to an alert from the USDA's Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS).

The not-ready-to-eat bacon, which is sold in three states, is produced by Maple Leaf Foods, Inc., located in Lisle, Illinois. It was distributed to grocery distributors and retailers in Idaho, Oregon and Washington.

Fox News Digital reached out to Maple Leaf Foods requesting comment.

The bacon was recalled because it was imported from Canada without undergoing a required U.S. import inspection, the USDA stated in its July 24 alert. 

The issue was discovered during routine inspection activities.

The USDA classified this as a Class I recall, its most serious category of recalls. 

The FSIS defines a Class I recall as a "health hazard situation where there is a reasonable probability that the use of the product will cause serious, adverse health consequences or death."

The Class I designation reflects the potential risk posed by the inspection failure, but does not indicate any confirmed illnesses linked to consumption of the bacon.

The recalled products — produced on June 9, June 10, June 12, June 13 and June 15, 2026 — include the following, per the USDA alert. 

The recalled product has the Canadian establishment number "EST. 1" printed on the side of the package, and the health certificate "2026-S732971612" on the master case boxes, the USDA's alert states.

Anyone who has any of these products in their fridge or freezer should throw them away or return them to the place where they were purchased, health officials advised.

item.title: Burma approves death penalty for scammers months after FBI's $8 billion crypto crackdown
item.description: Burma's new law mandates the death penalty for internet scammers months after the FBI's $8 billion Bitcoin seizure from a criminal network.
item.content:encoded:
Burma's government approved the death penalty as punishment for internet scammers just months after the FBI announced a sweeping $8 billion crackdown on scam networks coming from the country, according to the country's state-backed media.

The Anti-Online Scam Law passed the country's parliament on Tuesday, green lighting the death penalty for anyone who participates in a scam in which they "commit violence, torture, unlawfully arrest or detain, or treat any person in a cruel manner," according to The Global New Light of Myanmar, a media outlet jointly operated by a private company and the country's Ministry of the Interior.

Burma, also known as Myanmar, has become ground zero for digital scams, with criminals often recruiting migrants from other Asian countries with promises of legitimate work only to imprison them and force them to conduct the scams.

In May, the FBI announced a massive crackdown on a criminal network in Burma known as the "Democratic Karen Benevolent Army." The operation resulted in the seizure of 127,000 Bitcoin, worth over $8 billion as of July.

FBI BRINGS ALLEGED CHINA-LINKED HACKER TO US IN RARE EXTRADITION AS PATEL DEFENDS ITALY TRIP

The scammers, who allegedly have ties to Chinese organized crime, had been specifically targeting Americans in their operations, extracting over $3 million from one elderly American, the FBI previously told Fox News Digital.

In 2025, Chinese, Thai and Burmese authorities liberated more than 7,000 people from locked compounds in Burma.

NEW GERMANY SEX-CRIME FIGURES REIGNITE MIGRATION FIGHT AS EXPLOITATION PROBE EXPANDS

While the new Anti-Online Scam Law only mandates the death penalty for offenses that lead to another person's death, the law mandates 10 years in prison for any instance of forced labor in relation to cybercrime.

The law's approval also comes two days before the United Nations International Organization for Migration's World Day Against Trafficking in Persons. This year the international body will commemorate the day on July 30 under the theme "Trapped Behind the Scam."

"People trapped in scam compounds are victims of trafficking, forced to commit crimes through violence, threats and coercion. They deserve protection, not punishment," IOM Director General Amy Pope said in a statement. "We must work together to support survivors, stop traffickers and close the gaps these criminal networks exploit. No country can tackle this alone."

The United Nations estimates that South Pacific scams resulted in the loss of over $114 billion in 2025.

Pulte on Sunday had announced the completion of a fourth batch of layoffs from the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI).

"Since becoming Acting Director of National Intelligence, our team has been smartly, and carefully, reducing the size of ODNI, re-focusing ODNI on national security, the law, and the statute. As of this evening, we just finished a 4th round of thoughtful, measured layoffs. Thank you!" he declared in a Sunday night post on X.

In a July 10 post, he had stated, "U.S. National Intelligence is operating more efficiently and effectively than ever before, and today, we started a third round of reducing redundant, or non-critical, personnel. DNI’s future is exceptionally bright, and will be focused on following the law and the statute."

Pulte, the director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency, took on the role of acting DNI last month as Tulsi Gabbard, who had been serving as DNI, departed the role due to her husband's cancer battle.

TRUMP'S DNI PICK JAY CLAYTON LOCKS HORNS WITH DEMOCRATIC SENATOR IN FIERY CONFIRMATION HEARING CLASH

Prior to when Pulte took the helm at ODNI last month, The Wall Street Journal reported that during an interview, President Donald Trump said he had informed Pulte that he thought the ODNI was "unnecessary and/or too big."

"I'd like to see it smaller. I think there are a lot of people in there that shouldn’t be there," the president said, pointing to Obama and Biden administration carryovers, according to the Journal. Asked if he was calling on Pulte to terminate workers, the president stated that he wanted Pulte to "start the process," noting that the eventual DNI nominee should carry on that effort, the outlet reported.

In part of a June Truth Social post, Trump declared, "I have named William Pulte to be Acting Director of National Intelligence, who will take over on June 19th, and have asked him to execute the immediate and needed downsizing of the office, reverting staff to their home agencies."

Fox News Digital reached out to ODNI on Tuesday asking for clarification on the reported 30% staffing reduction.

SENATE CLEARS WAY FOR TRUMP'S TOP SPY AS KEY ANTI-TERROR PROGRAM REMAINS IN LIMBO

Sen. Tom Cotton, R-Ark., said during a Senate floor speech last month that he had spoken with the acting DNI, who he says agreed "that we need to return the ODNI to its original size, scope, and mission by spinning off some of these functional... centers and sending intelligence officers who have been detailed there back to their home agencies so they can do actual intelligence work."

"He informed me that yes, a small handful of front office personnel are leaving federal employment, which is not at all uncommon when a senior leader leaves an agency or one comes into an agency," Cotton said. "He also said that a few dozen, around 45 or 50, career officers are, in fact, returning to their home agencies."

Trump last month announced that he was tapping U.S. District Attorney for the Southern District of New York Jay Clayton as his DNI nominee.

The Senate is slated to vote on confirming Clayton on Tuesday night.

item.title: Thousands swarm stunning mountain escape as selfie tourism backlash erupts online
item.description: Photos are showing massive shuttle lines at Tre Cime di Lavaredo in Italy as selfie tourism overwhelms one of the Dolomites' most iconic destinations for travelers.
item.content:encoded:
The pursuit of the perfect selfie is creating headaches for one of the Italian Alps' most recognizable landmarks.

Viral videos shared online in recent weeks show massive crowds stretching through shuttle queues as visitors wait to reach Tre Cime di Lavaredo, one of the most iconic destinations in Italy's Dolomites.

The videos have sparked outrage, with many online commenters arguing that visitors were more interested in taking photos than enjoying the mountains.

FAMOUS BEACH NOW REQUIRES VISITORS TO RESERVE SPOTS WEEKS AHEAD AND PAY FEES

"This video proves that people are no longer able to enjoy the journey," one commenter wrote on Instagram. "In their minds, the only thing that matters is the photo."

"Everyone lined up for a photo just to show people on social media how great their lives are," said another user. "Hours in line for one picture."

Tre Cime di Lavaredo is one of the most famous landmarks in the Dolomites. It draws visitors from around the world with its trio of mountain peaks.

The UNESCO-protected mountains are subject to the Enrosadira phenomenon, in which sunrise and sunset turn the rock walls a vibrant pink and orange, according to The Dolomites — UNESCO World Heritage Centre page. 

Tre Cime di Lavaredo gets over 800,000 visitors per year, per the Tre Cime di Lavaredo Hike Guide.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Hikers and climbers gravitate to legendary vertical rock faces in summer, while winter transforms the region into a massive and interconnected ski network, according to Dolomites.com.

In response to the growing crowds, officials are considering requiring reservations for shuttle passengers in addition to the reservation system already in place for drivers.

Drivers must reserve access to the Rifugio Auronzo parking area in advance, according to the reservation website.

Reservations cost €40 (about $45) for cars, €26 (about $30) for motorcycles and €60 (about $68) for camper vans.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

Tre Cime is not the only destination in the Dolomites that's been grappling with issues caused by overtourism.

Landowners near Seceda, another popular mountain destination in the Dolomites, reinstated €5 (around $5.60) turnstiles to help manage growing crowds at one of the region's most photographed viewpoints, as Fox News Digital previously reported.

Carlo Zanella, president of the Alto Adige Alpine Club, previously told Fox News Digital that the turnstiles were installed by a local farmer after visitors repeatedly trampled meadows while flocking to the scenic overlook.

Zanella also criticized the role of social media in reshaping mountain tourism.

"I am against the influencers," he said. "They are only interested in making money [through] advertising."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Zanella encouraged visitors to explore lesser-known areas of the Dolomites, saying there are "other even more beautiful places to visit."

Ashley DiMella of Fox News Digital contributed reporting.

item.title: Chevy Chase called out for being 'not so nice' to Billy Joel's ex-wife at a keg party
item.description: Katie Lee Biegel claimed on her podcast that Chevy Chase mistook her for staff and shooed her away at a keg party with her ex-husband Billy Joel.
item.content:encoded:
Billy Joel's ex-wife has called out Chevy Chase for being "not-so-nice" during an old-school keg party.

Katie Lee Biegel addressed the incident on a recent episode of her podcast, "All on the Table." She explained that the incident with Chase happened while she was married to Joel. The former couple tied the knot in 2004 before divorcing in 2009.

"My celebrity run-in that was not so nice was Chevy Chase," Biegel began.

"So, I was having a party with my ex-husband. It was a keg party. I wanted to have like an old-school keg party. We had a house that we were going to tear down. And it was like this little — we called it ‘The Sugar Shack,’ and had a very fun summer there, staying with friends," Biegel said.

JOEL MCHALE DISLOCATED CHEVY CHASE'S SHOULDER WHILE FILMING 'COMMUNITY'

She continued, "But then at the end of the summer, we decided to have a kind of like, ‘Tear the House Down' party, a keg party, and I had jello shots, kegs. It was a very star-studded party."

Biegel went on to explain the moment Chase mistook her for a member of the staff and "shooed" her away.

"And my ex-husband was standing talking to Chevy Chase and his wife. And I had a tray of jello shots. And I went up with the tray of jello shots and said, you know, ‘Do you guys want a shot?’ and Chevy thought that I was the staff at the party, and he took his hand and shooed me away," she said.

LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"He just did this," she said, making a shooing motion with her hand.

Chase has long had a reputation in Hollywood for being difficult to work with, with multiple former co-stars and collaborators alleging abrasive, confrontational and inappropriate behavior over the years.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

His most public controversies stem from his time on "Community," where he clashed with creator Dan Harmon and several cast members before leaving the show in 2012 after reportedly using racially insensitive language on set.

Fox News Digital reached out to Chase for comment.

item.title: Anthony Fauci diary entries set social media ablaze as critics mock, condemn behavior
item.description: Dr. Anthony Fauci's diary entries reveal his fixation on fame and media appearances during the COVID pandemic, sparking massive social media backlash.
item.content:encoded:
Once-private diary entries written by Dr. Anthony Fauci have set social media ablaze with critics mocking the former White House COVID advisor’s fixation on emerging from the global pandemic as a celebrity and condemning his behavior. 

Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee Chairman Rand Paul, R-Ky., made the diaries public as part of the committee's ongoing oversight investigation. The journals chronicle Fauci's day-to-day role during the COVID-19 crisis through conversations with President Donald Trump, governors and world leaders, while detailing his media appearances and personal observations. 

While much of the mainstream media initially ignored the shocking diary entries, there was no shortage of backlash on X. Outkick founder Clay Travis urged his followers to read the diary, calling Fauci "one of the true villains of American history." 

ABC, NBC, CBS, CNN AND MS NOW IGNORE FAUCI DIARY ENTRIES THAT REVEAL FIXATION ON FAME DURING COVID

Grabien Media founder Tom Elliott, who spent hours digging into the diary, found that the word "award" was mentioned 80 times, "hero" appeared 49 times, "press" appeared a staggering 641 times and Fauci never wrote anything about "peer review," "meta-analysis," "risk-benefit," "learning loss" or "mental health."

Dana Loesch was stunned, calling the diary "one of the most infuriating things I’ve ever read." 

Piers Morgan added, "These diaries are very damning. Fauci comes across as a fame-hungry narcissist who regularly said different things in private about Covid to what he told the world publicly."

FAUCI'S NEWLY RELEASED COVID DIARIES REVEAL BIZARRE FIXATION ON FAME AS PANDEMIC DEATHS MOUNTED

Others put a spotlight on Fauci's apparent love for the TV camera. 

XX-XY founder Jennifer Sey unearthed an old Politico appearance in which Fauci simply read flattering tweets about himself. 

"Hard hitting stuff here," Sey snarked. "Could you kiss his butt anymore?"

FAUCI'S DIARY SHOWS HE FED QUESTIONS TO JOURNALISTS, BUILT FRIENDSHIPS WITH MEDIA FIGURES

Many comments were focused on Fauci's relationship with CNN anchor Jake Tapper, who appeared to be the doctor's closest media ally.  

The diary release came days before Fauci is scheduled to testify before the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee after being subpoenaed by Paul, who also took to X to lampoon the diary. The senator shared an AI-generated image of Fauci sitting on a bed while writing in a diary. In the background are posters and toys in a humorous attempt to suggest the doctor was like a self-obsessed teenager. Next to the image, Paul wrote: "What Anthony Fauci looked like every night when he wrote about how great he is in his diary."

Fox News Digital reached out to Dr. Fauci and CNN for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

Fox News Digital’s Amanda Macias contributed to this report.

item.title: Patriots receiver Mack Hollins’ barefoot escapades reach a new plateau in second New England season
item.description: Mack Hollins says New England restaurants now let him dine barefoot after his breakout Patriots season, but his shoeless habit is just one quirk.
item.content:encoded:
Mack Hollins has turned the proverbial corner as a New England Patriots wide receiver, but not in the ordinary way one might think, like his speed is improved or he reads defenders better now. This is more about his feet.

His habitually unapologetic bare feet.

Hollins reports that in his second year on the Patriots roster, his life habit of walking everywhere in his bare feet has gained acceptance locally. He knows this because restaurants are welcoming him in and allowing him to dine – sans shoes.

MACK HOLLINS ENTERS STADIUM WITH NO SHOES OR SHIRT

"I love it," Hollins told reporters at Patriots training camp during an interview session conducted barefoot. "It's really great because now they're kind of letting me slide being barefoot in restaurants and stuff because they know who I am.

"At first, it was like, some homeless guy coming in here, but now it's like the mechanic homeless guy so it's all right. So yeah, it's been great."

Let this marinate.

If you're pretty much disgusted by somebody else's bare feet on display anywhere but a beach, you're not going to be a fan. If you're thinking this is an attention-seeking move, well, maybe. Hollins has been known to stand out and not shy from attention.

ROB GRONKOWSKI OFFERS ADVICE FOR PATRIOTS TO SILENCE NOISE AROUND MIKE VRABEL CONTROVERSY AHEAD OF 2026 SEASON

But if you're a Patriots' fan and watched last season when Hollins unexpectedly started 13 regular-season games and two postseason games, and scored the team's only touchdown on a 35-yard reception in the Super Bowl LX, you might be more accepting of the guy's eccentricities.

And Hollins has a few.

He doesn't, for example, use forks or spoons or chopsticks or any other eating utensils. He uses his hands to eat because, he says, it helps him correctly gauge the temperature of the food which prepares his mouth for what's coming.

So, these New England restaurants are showing love to the barefoot guy who eats with his hands.

"Every team I've been on, you ask them who's the weirdest guy they're going to say Mack," Hollins once admitted.

But this isn't aloof weird.

Or disruptive weird.

It's perhaps endearing weird.

"Yeah, yeah, it's not like a bad weird," Hollins said.

It's weird like Hollins showing up to NFL games in Buffalo's frigid temperatures shirtless. Also barefoot, of course, despite the ice and snow on the ground.

It's weird like him arriving to the 2025 AFC Championship game between the Bills and Kansas City Chiefs wearing an Animal Muppet character — you know, the red thing that plays drums — mask.

All that aside, shoeless Mack Hollins is gaining traction in New England. And he has an explanation why he prefers to do without footgear when he's not actually in a game.

"I think shoes are a tool and people have made them a part of their body," Hollins once said. "I wouldn't walk around with a hammer just because I might need a hammer sometimes."

item.title: What a fourth-generation fishing captain has learned from nearly 100 years on the Gulf
item.description: Dylan Hubbard carries nearly 100 years of family legacy at Hubbard's Marina in Madeira Beach, navigating hurricanes, NOAA and a changing industry.
item.content:encoded:
For Dylan Hubbard, fishing is the easy part.

The harder part is carrying nearly 100 years of family history on his shoulders while figuring out how to keep the operation alive through hurricanes, federal regulators and a rapidly changing Florida tourism industry.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK

Hubbard is the fourth generation of his family to run Hubbard's Marina in Madeira Beach, Fla. The business traces its roots to 1928, when his grandfather started with five rowboats and 40 cane poles.

Today, Hubbard is vice president of the company and has begun the process of purchasing it from his father. But stepping into the family business was never as simple as inheriting a title.

"Oh, you have no idea," Hubbard told OutKick Outdoors when asked whether he had to earn his place before calling himself captain.

His grandfather, Wilson, originally ran the operation before leaving to serve during World War II. Hubbard's great-grandfather stepped in during that time, which is why the family considers it a fourth-generation business. His father later purchased the company from the family in 2004. Now, Dylan is preparing to carry it forward.

"It's also really cool to have that layer of: it's a family business. I'm fourth generation," Hubbard said. "Not only am I working, but also it's that legacy. So it's just an added layer of maybe responsibility or honor or blessing — whatever you want to call it — that really makes it even that much more special."

Watch Dylan Hubbard's full interview with OutKick Outdoors here:

That responsibility means knowing when to hold onto tradition and when to embrace change.

Hubbard's Marina began in Pass-a-Grille, back when Florida's barrier islands looked very different. But as new bridges changed traffic patterns and Pass-a-Grille became increasingly residential, Hubbard's grandfather recognized that the business needed a new home. Even though he was nearing 70 years old, he uprooted the operation and moved it north to John's Pass.

"He saw the writing on the wall," Hubbard said.

It was the kind of decision that probably felt risky at the time but proved essential in the decades that followed. John's Pass eventually developed into a major tourism destination, and Hubbard's grandfather also worked with the city to establish the boardwalk that now runs through the area.

That willingness to adapt has remained necessary — especially when nature delivered its worst, twice in less than two weeks.

In September 2024, Hurricane Helene brought nine feet of water into Hubbard's Marina. The main office was completely submerged, the main dock was destroyed, and the business lost infrastructure, inventory and equipment. Before the water had even fully receded, Hurricane Milton was bearing down as a Category 5, forcing the family to brace for a second direct hit while still standing in the wreckage of the first.

"It was pretty numbing," Hubbard said, "just a wild situation to go through."

Still, the boats survived. More importantly, so did the people.

Before official rescue crews could even reach the barrier islands, Hubbard and several crew members set out before daylight to assess the damage at John's Pass. What began as a trip to inspect the business quickly became something else entirely.

"We were the first boat out there," Hubbard said. "No one was out there — no fire, no EMS, no emergency folks. It was just us."

As they navigated through the damaged area, residents stood along seawalls crying, waving and begging for help. Some had stayed behind during the storm, become trapped, and then emerged to find they had lost everything.

"So what was supposed to be a search and find out what we needed to do and what got damaged turned into a rescue mission," Hubbard said.

Other members of the fishing community soon joined in, deploying their own boats to move people and supplies to and from the barrier islands — even as police tried, unsuccessfully, to keep boaters off the water given the debris and damage.

"We were essentially pirates for a week," he said.

For Hubbard, reopening quickly was never primarily about preserving the business's reputation or getting tourists back on boats. It was about his employees. At the time, the company had 84 staff members. Fifteen had lost everything in the storm.

"If I had just sat there and waited and not got to work, those people would not only have lost their homes and their vehicles and everything they owned, they would have also lost their jobs and not had income," Hubbard said. "So to me, it was imperative to open up as quickly as humanly possible."

The team rebuilt the dock in two days and had trips running again five days after Helene — faster than the barrier islands themselves officially reopened. The community later raised nearly $75,000 to help affected staff members.

In the year that followed, Hubbard's kept growing rather than pulling back: the company acquired a pirate ship, a dolphin tour boat and a shark tour operation in November 2025, adding to a portfolio that already includes a seafood market, a fuel dock and a boat-building operation. A new ghost tour just launched, and a Tampa Bay ferry service is next.

Capt. Hubbard may prefer being offshore, but much of his job now happens behind a desk, in meetings, or fighting battles that never make it onto a dock report.

Hubbard is heavily involved in fisheries management, serving as president of the Florida Guides Association and sitting on Gulf Council advisory panels covering reef fish, data collection and outreach.

A few years ago, that involvement got personal. After Hubbard publicly criticized weak enforcement against illegal charter operations at a federal meeting, NOAA's Office of Law Enforcement took a closer look at his own business — and told him the way Hubbard's Marina operated was against federal regulation.

It took him roughly 85 days to get the regulation itself changed, preserving his business model in the process.

"If you're not in the room, you're on the menu," Hubbard said of why he keeps showing up to meetings most people would find, in his words, "mind-numbing and boring."

CHARTER CAPTAIN JONATHAN MOSS EXPLAINS HOW TO GET KIDS HOOKED ON FISHING FROM AN EARLY AGE

It's not the only wild thing nearly 100 years on the Gulf has produced. Ask Hubbard for his strangest moment on the water and the answer comes without hesitation: "We've found dead bodies. We've come across boats on fire. We've saved people." His grandfather ran across great white sharks; his father, orcas; Hubbard himself has crossed paths with pilot whales, a right whale and one of the largest leatherback turtles he's ever seen.

"People always ask me, 'Do you still get to go fishing?'" Hubbard said. "I do, and I make time for it, and I definitely get out on the water as much as I can."

But he also understands that spending all his time fishing wouldn't necessarily serve the larger operation.

"If I spent my time offshore, that's definitely where I would rather be and enjoy a lot more," he said. "But I definitely wouldn't be in the position we are today if I did that all the time."

Hubbard hopes his grandfather would approve of where the family business stands today.

"I hope he would be happy," Hubbard said.

The pirate ship, the ferry, the federal meetings — none of that existed when Wilson Hubbard started with five rowboats. But the motto he built the business on hasn't changed.

"If you're too busy to go fishing, you're just too darn busy."

Still true, four generations later.
